A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FTTT and OPTUNE work. All 13 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reasoning and code-generation experiments, scaling curves, architecture ablations, case studies and training curves.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds cross-dataset transfer results in Appendix D, Table 6.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the losses, gradient compression and decomposition, and OPTUNE architecture are retained. The added explanations of single-step optimization and updates clarify the existing procedure without establishing an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: The same four datasets remain, but Appendix D adds cross-dataset transfer scenarios: MATH-trained OPTUNE evaluated on GSM8K and MBPP-trained OPTUNE evaluated on HumanEval. This extends evaluation to datasets unseen during optimizer training without adding domains.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 retain the same test-time scaling and fine-tuning comparators. Table 6 reuses raw-model baselines whose four scores match the existing Best-of-N entries in Table 2; no new comparison algorithm is introduced.

E3.justification: Appendix D introduces training on one dataset and testing on another. Existing benchmark settings, including greedy-decoding failure subsets, metrics, models and the tables' budget of 32, remain unchanged. The new transfer experiment does not explicitly specify its budget.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a transferability analysis testing whether the learned optimizer remains useful on another dataset. Existing self-reflection comparisons, architecture ablations, scaling analyses, case studies and training curves are retained.

E5.justification: Tables 2 and 3 retain three-seed means and standard deviations, and the scaling-curve reporting and Spearman correlation test are unchanged. Table 6 adds point scores without introducing a new uncertainty estimate or repeated-run procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 retain their results. New Table 6 reports transfer OPTUNE scores of 0.8914/0.7037 for Llama and 0.7921/0.7100 for Mistral on GSM8K/HumanEval, respectively, against raw-model scores of 0.8069/0.6728 and 0.7807/0.6500. These are new transfer results, not improvements over matched v1 experiments.

T1.justification: The equations, gradient decomposition, Markov formulation and convergence statement are retained. The independent-update assumption now says 'weight matrix' instead of 'parameter,' clarifying the already matrix-valued Wi formulation. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: feedback-based test-time training and an efficient learned optimizer with improved reasoning performance and scaling. The transfer appendix does not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains the restriction to one-step optimization through non-differentiable generation, adds rationale about gradients encoding weight information and rank reduction/dropout mitigating overfitting, and interprets Table 6 as evidence of transfer potential. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents one FTTT update per attempt, one-step optimizer training, feedback-based answer selection for Revision, and use of the final-epoch checkpoint in Appendix A. These are additional disclosures; the PDFs do not establish that existing experiments changed or were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 adds Schmidhuber (1992) and Schlag et al. (2021) to the fast-weights discussion and references. It also explicitly contrasts gradient-based compression with resource-intensive black-box optimization using the already cited Chen et al. (2017). The main related-work positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Changes are localized explanatory additions and wording corrections. Section 4.2 changes from 'Training-Free Results' to 'Test-Time Scaling Results,' Appendix C becomes 'Training Curves,' and acknowledgments and Appendix D are added. The overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 6 and moves Figure 5 from PDF page 12 to page 13. Appendix reflow also keeps the Llama prompt box together instead of splitting it across pages. Existing figures and Tables 1–5 retain their displays and content.

improvement.justification: v2 adds bounded evidence for cross-dataset transfer that v1 lacked and improves reproducibility through checkpoint and optimization details. The design explanations also become clearer while the main evidence remains stable. Table 6's unspecified budget and uncertainty limit the strength of the added transfer evidence, so the overall gain is modest.
